G3000.def:
λατρεύω
(λάτρις, a hired servant), [in LXX (always, as λατρεία, of the service of God or of heathen divinities) chiefly for עָבַד, Exode 3:12, al.; in Dan LXX TH (Daniel 3:12, al.) for פְּלַח ;] 
__1. to work for hire. 
__2. to serve; in cl., also of divine service, to serve, worship, and so always in NT: with dative of person(s), τ. θεῷ, Matthieu 4:10, Luc 4:8" (LXX), Actes 7:7 24:14 27:23, Hébreux 9:14, Apocalypse 7:15 22:3; of idol worship (cf. Exode 20:5, Eze.20:32), Actes 7:42, Romains 1:25; τ. θεῷ. ἐν τ. πνεύματί μου, Romains 1:9; id. ἐν καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, 2 Timothée 1:3; μετ᾽ εὐλαβείας κ. δέους, Hébreux 12:28; ἐν ὁσιότητι κ. δικαιοσύνῃ, Luc 1:74; (without θεῷ) νηστείαις κ. δεήσεσι, Luc 2:37; πνεύματι θεοῦ, Philippiens 3:3; absol., Actes 26:7; ὁ λατρεύων, the worshipper, Hébreux 9:9 10:2; of ministerial service, with dative of thing(s), Hébreux 8:5 13:10.†
SYN.: λειτουργέω, q.v

G3001.def:
λάχανον, -ου, τό
(λαχαίνω, to dig), [in LXX: Genèse 9:3; 3Ki.21:2, Psaumes 37:2, Proverbes 15:17 (יֶרֶק, יָרָק) * ;] 
a garden herb, vegetable: Luc 11:42; usually in pl., Matthieu 13:32, Marc 4:32, Romains 14:2.†
SYN.: βοτάνη, q.v

G3002.def:
λεββαῖος, -ου, ὁ
(on the derivation, see Dalman, Words, 50; Swete, Mk., l.with), 
Lebbæus: Matthieu 10:3, Marc 3:18 (WH, mg.; Θαδδαῖος, which see, Rec., WH, txt., RV, cf. WH, App., 11, 24. In Luc 6:15, Actes 1:13, he is called Σίμων ὁ Ζηλωτής.)†

G3003.def:
λεγιών (Rec. -εών), -ῶνος, ἡ, (Lat. legio), 
a legion: Matthieu 26:53, Marc 5:9, 15, Luc 8:30.†

G3004G.def:
λέγω, 
[in LXX very freq., chiefly for אמר; λέγει for נְאֻם, Genèse 22:16, al. ;] 
__1. in Hom., to pick out, gather, reckon, recount.
__2. In Hdt. and Att., to say, speak, affirm, declare: absol., Actes 13:15, 24:10; before orat. dir., Matthieu 9:34, Marc 3:11, Jean 1:29, al.; before ὅτι recit., Marc 3:21, Luc 1:24, Jean 6:14, al.; accusative and inf., Luc 11:18, Jean 12:29, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, Matthieu 11:17, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), Matthieu 25:9, Marc 3:33, 7:28, Luc 24:6, 7, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Matthieu 3:9, Luc 3:8, al.; of writing, 2 Corinthiens 8:8, Philippiens 4:11, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή, Romains 4:3, Jacques 2:23, al.; with accusative of thing(s), Luc 8:8, 9:33, Jean 5:34, al.; σὺ λέγεις (a non-committal phrase; Swete, Mk., 359, 369f.), Matthieu 27:11, Marc 15:2, Luc 23:3, Jean 18:37; with dative of person(s), before orat. dir., Matthieu 8:20, Marc 2:17, al. mult.; id. before ὅτι, Matthieu 3:9, al.; with prep., πρός, μετά, περί, etc., Marc 4:41, Jean 11:56, Hébreux 9:5, al.; to mean (cl.), Marc 14:71, Jean 6:71, 1 Corinthiens 10:29, al.; to call, name, Marc 10:18; pass., Matthieu 9:9, Marc 15:7, al (cf. ἀντι-, δια- (-μαι), προ-, συλ-λέγω). 
SYN.: λαλέω, which refers to the utterance, as λέγω to the meaning of what is said, its correspondence with thought (Tr., Syn., Ixxvi; Thayer, see word λαλέω).

G3004H.def:
λέγω, 
[in LXX very freq., chiefly for אמר; λέγει for נְאֻם, Genèse 22:16, al. ;] 
__1. in Hom., to pick out, gather, reckon, recount.
__2. In Hdt. and Att., to say, speak, affirm, declare: absol., Actes 13:15, 24:10; before orat. dir., Matthieu 9:34, Marc 3:11, Jean 1:29, al.; before ὅτι recit., Marc 3:21, Luc 1:24, Jean 6:14, al.; accusative and inf., Luc 11:18, Jean 12:29, al.; after another verb of speaking, προσφωνεῖν κ. λέγειν, Matthieu 11:17, al.; ἀπεκρίθη (ἐλάλησεν) λέγων (καὶ λέγει; Dalman, Words, 24 ff.), Matthieu 25:9, Marc 3:33, 7:28, Luc 24:6, 7, al.; of unspoken thought, λ. ἐν ἑαυτῷ, Matthieu 3:9, Luc 3:8, al.; of writing, 2 Corinthiens 8:8, Philippiens 4:11, al.; λέγει ἡ γραφή, Romains 4:3, Jacques 2:23, al.; with accusative of thing(s), Luc 8:8, 9:33, Jean 5:34, al.; σὺ λέγεις (a non-committal phrase; Swete, Mk., 359, 369f.), Matthieu 27:11, Marc 15:2, Luc 23:3, Jean 18:37; with dative of person(s), before orat. dir., Matthieu 8:20, Marc 2:17, al. mult.; id. before ὅτι, Matthieu 3:9, al.; with prep., πρός, μετά, περί, etc., Marc 4:41, Jean 11:56, Hébreux 9:5, al.; to mean (cl.), Marc 14:71, Jean 6:71, 1 Corinthiens 10:29, al.; to call, name, Marc 10:18; pass., Matthieu 9:9, Marc 15:7, al (cf. ἀντι-, δια- (-μαι), προ-, συλ-λέγω). 
SYN.: λαλέω, which refers to the utterance, as λέγω to the meaning of what is said, its correspondence with thought (Tr., Syn., Ixxvi; Thayer, see word λαλέω).

G3005.def:
λεῖμμα (WH, λίμμα, see their App., 154), -τος, τό
(λείπω), [in LXX: 4Ki.19:4 A (שְׁאֵרִית)* ;] 
a remnant: Romains 11:5.†

G3006.def:
λεῖος, -εία, -εῖον 
[in LXX: Genèse 27:11, 1 Rois 17:40 R (חָלַק, חַלֻּק); ὁδὸς λ., Ésaïe 40:4 Α (בִּקְעָה); Proverbes 2:20 12:13 26:23 * ;] 
smooth: opposite to τραχύς, Luc 3:5 (LXX).†

G3007.def:
λείπω 
[in LXX: Job 4:11, Proverbes 19:4 (פָּרַד), al. ;] 
__1. trans., to leave, leave behind; pass., to be left behind, to lack before prep. (as more usual in cl.), ἐν, Jacques 1:4; with genitive of thing(s), Jacques 1:5 2:15. 
__2. Intrans., to be gone, to be wanting: with dative of person(s), Luc 18:22, Tite 3:13; τὰ λείποντα, Tite 1:5 
(cf. ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, ἐν-κατα-, περι-, ὑπο-λείπω).†

G3008.def:
λειτουργέω, -ῶ
(λειτουργός), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁרַת pi., also for עָבַד, צָבָא, etc. ;] 
__1. in cl., at Athens, to supply public offices at one's own cost, render public service to the State, hence, generally, 
__2. to serve the State, do a service, serve (of service to the Gods, Diod., i, 21): of the official service of priests and Levites (Exode 29:30, Nombres 16:9, Sir.4:14, 1Ma.10:42, al.; cf. Deiss., BS, 140 f.), Hébreux 10:11; of Christians: with dative of person(s) before ἐν, Romains 15:27 (cf. Sir.10:25); τ. κυρίῳ, Actes 13:2.†
SYN.: λατρεύω (which see), prop., to serve for hire, LXX (as some­times in cl.), always of service to the deity on the part of both priests and people (Exode 4:3, Deutéronome 10:12, and similarly in NT). λειτουργέω "is the fulfilment of an office: it has a definite representative character, and corresponds with a function to be discharged". It is therefore used of serving in an office or ministry: in LXX always of priests and Levites, in NT, with its cognates (Romains 13:6 15:27, are not really exceptions), of services rendered either to God or man by apostles, prophets, teachers, and other officers of the church (cf. Tr., Syn., § xxxv; ICC on Romains 1:9; Westc., He., 232 ff.)

G3009.def:
λειτουργία, -ας, ἡ
(λειτουργέω), [in LXX chiefly for עֲבֹדָה, Nombres 4:24, 1 Chroniques 9:13, al. ;] 
__1. in cl. (chiefly of Athens), the discharge of a public office at one's own expense (see LS, see word), hence, 
__2. a service, ministry; in π. (Deiss., BS, 140 f.) and in LXX (though here also of secular service, 3Ki.1:4, al.), of religious service or ministration; and so in NT: of priestly ministrations, Luc 1:23, Hébreux 8:6 9:21; figuratively, θυσία καὶ λ. τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν, Philippiens 2:17; of Christian beneficence, 2 Corinthiens 9:12, Philippiens 2:30.†

G3010.def:
λειτουργικός, -ή, -όν 
[in LXX for עֲבֹדָה, שָׁרַת; ἔργα, Num_7:5; στολαί Exode 31:10 39:32; σκευή, Nombres 4:12, 26, 2 Chroniques 24:14 * ;] 
of or for service, ministering: πνεύματα, Hébreux 1:14.†

G3011.def:
λειτουργός, -οῦ, ὁ
(λιός, ἔργον), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁרַת, Josué 1:1 A, 3Ki.10:5, Psaumes 103:21, Sir.7:30, al. ;] 
__1. in cl., one who discharges a public office at his own expense, then, generally, 
__2. a public servant, a minister, servant: τ. ἁγίων λ., Hébreux 8:2 (cf. Néhémie 10:39, Sir, l.with); Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, Romains 15:16; pl., τ. θεοῦ, Romains 13:6, Hébreux 1:7" (LXX) ; λ. ὑμῶν τ. χρείας μου, Philippiens 2:25.†
SYN.: see: διάκονος, λειτουργέω

G3012.def:
λέντιον, -ου, τό (Lat. linteum), 
a linen cloth, towel: Jean 13:4-5.†

G3013.def:
λεπίς, -ίδος, ἡ
(λέπω, to peel) [in LXX chiefly for קַשְׂקֶשֶׂת ;] 
a scale: Actes 9:18†

G3014.def:
λέπρα, -ας, ἡ
(λεπρός), [in LXX for צָרַעַת ;] 
leprosy: Matthieu 8:3, Marc 1:42, Luc 5:12-13†

G3015.def:
λεπρός, -ά, -όν
(λεπίς), [in LXX for צָרַע ;] 
__1. (in cl.) scaly, rough. 
__2. leprous; chiefly as subst., ὁ λ., a leper: Matthieu 8:2 10:8 11:5, Marc 1:40, Luc 4:27 7:22 17:12; of Simon, formerly a leper, Matthieu 26:6, Marc 14:3.†

G3016.def:
λεπτός, -ή, -όν
(λέπω, to peel), 
__1. peeled. 
__2. fine, thin, small, light; hence, in late Gk., as subst. τὸ λ., a small coin (one-eighth of an as, AV, mite): Marc 12:42, Luc 12:59 21:2.†

G3017G.def:
Λευεί (indecl.) and Λευείς (Rec. -υΐ, -υΐς), genitive Λευεί, accusative -είν, ὁ (Heb. H3878) 
Levi; 
__1. the son of Jacob: Hébreux 7:5, 9, Apocalypse 7:7. 
__2. Son of Melchi: Luc 3:24. 
__3. Son of Simeon: Luc 3:29. 
__4. Son of Alphæus (cf. Μαθθαῖος): Marc 2:14 (WH, mg., Ἰάκωβον), Luc 5:27, 29.†

G3017H.def:
Λευεί (indecl.) and Λευείς (Rec. -υΐ, -υΐς), genitive Λευεί, accusative -είν, ὁ (Heb. H3878) 
Levi; 
__1. the son of Jacob: Hébreux 7:5, 9, Apocalypse 7:7. 
__2. Son of Melchi: Luc 3:24. 
__3. Son of Simeon: Luc 3:29. 
__4. Son of Alphæus (cf. Μαθθαῖος): Marc 2:14 (WH, mg., Ἰάκωβον), Luc 5:27, 29.†

G3017I.def:
Λευεί (indecl.) and Λευείς (Rec. -υΐ, -υΐς), genitive Λευεί, accusative -είν, ὁ (Heb. H3878) 
Levi; 
__1. the son of Jacob: Hébreux 7:5, 9, Apocalypse 7:7. 
__2. Son of Melchi: Luc 3:24. 
__3. Son of Simeon: Luc 3:29. 
__4. Son of Alphæus (cf. Μαθθαῖος): Marc 2:14 (WH, mg., Ἰάκωβον), Luc 5:27, 29.†

G3017J.def:
Λευεί (indecl.) and Λευείς (Rec. -υΐ, -υΐς), genitive Λευεί, accusative -είν, ὁ (Heb. H3878) 
Levi; 
__1. the son of Jacob: Hébreux 7:5, 9, Apocalypse 7:7. 
__2. Son of Melchi: Luc 3:24. 
__3. Son of Simeon: Luc 3:29. 
__4. Son of Alphæus (cf. Μαθθαῖος): Marc 2:14 (WH, mg., Ἰάκωβον), Luc 5:27, 29.†

G3019.def:
Λευείτης
(Rec. Λευΐτης), -ου, ὁ [in LXX for לֵוִיִּי ;] 
a Levite: Luc 10:32, Jean 1:19, Actes 4:36.†

G3020.def:
Λευειτικός
(Rec. Λευϊτ-), -ή, -όν [in LXX: Le, tit.* ;] 
Levitical: Hébreux 7:11.†

G3021.def:
λευκαίνω
(λευκός), [in LXX: Psaumes 51:7, Ésaïe 1:18 (לָבַן hi.), etc. ;] 
to whiten, make white: with accusative of thing(s), Marc 9:3, Apocalypse 7:14.†

G3022.def:
λευκο-βύσσινος, -ον
(cf. λευκολινής, a robe of white flax, C.I., 155, 17), 
white linen: Apocalypse 19:14 (WH, mg.).†
λευκός, ή, -όν 
[in LXX chiefly for לָבָן ;] 
__1. bright, brilliant: of clothing, Matthieu 17:2, Marc 9:3 16:5, Luc 9:29, Actes 1:10, Apocalypse 3:5 4:4 6:11 7:9, 13 19:14 (cf. Ecclésiaste 9:8); ὡς χιών, Matthieu 28:3; ἐν λ.. (sc. ἱματίοις), Jean 20:12, Apocalypse 3:4; θρόνος, Apocalypse 20:11. 
__2. white: Matthieu 5:36, Apocalypse 1:14 2:17 4:4 6:2 14:14 19:11; figuratively, of garments, Apocalypse 3:18; of ripened grain, Jean 4:35.†

G3023.def:
λέων, -οντος, ὁ 
[in LXX chiefly for אֲרִי, אַרְיֵה, also for כְּפִיר, etc. ;] 
a lion: Hébreux 11:33, 1 Pierre 5:8, Apocalypse 4:7 9:8, 17 10:3 13:2; metaphorically, 2 Timothée 4:17, Apocalypse 5:5.†

G3024.def:
λήθη, -ης, ἡ
(λήθω = λανθάνω) [in LXX: Lévitique 5:15 (מַעַל), Wis.16:11, Sir.14:7, al. ;] 
forgetfulness: λ. λαβεῖν (on the phrase, see Mayor, in l): 2 Pierre 1:9.†

G3025.def:
ληνός, -οῦ, ἡ
(in some MSS., LXX and NT, ὁ), [in LXX chiefly for יֶקֶב Nombres 18:27, al.; also for רַהַט (Genèse 30:38, 41), גַּת (Néhémie 13:15, al.), etc. ;] 
a trough or vat; esp. for the treading of grapes: Matthieu 21:33, Apocalypse 14:20 19:16; τὴν λ. . . . τὸν μέγαν (a solecism perhaps inadvertent), Apocalypse 14:19 (cf. ὑπολήνιον).†

G3026.def:
λῆρος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX: 4Ma.5:10 * ;] 
silly talk, nonsense: Luc 24:11.†

G3027.def:
λῃστής, -οῦ, ὁ
(Ep. ληίς = λεία, booty), [in LXX for גְּדוּד, etc. ;] 
a robber, brigand: Matthieu 21:13 (LXX) Matthieu 26:55 27:38, 44, Marc 11:17 14:48 15:27, Luc 10:30, 36 19:46 22:52, Jean 10:1, 8 18:40, 2 Corinthiens 11:26.†
SYN.: κλέπτης, q.v

G3028.def:
λῆμψις (Rec. λῆψις, so in cl.), -εως, ἡ 
(λαμβάνω), [in LXX (λῆψ-): Proverbes 15:29; λ. δώρων, Proverbes 15:27 (מַתָּנָה); λ. καὶ δόσις, Sir.41:19 42:7 * ;] 
receiving: δόσις καὶ λ., Philippiens 4:15.†

G3029.def:
λίαν, 
adv. [in LXX chiefly for מְאֹד Genèse 1:31 4:5, Jérémie 24:3, al.; Tob.9:4, 2Ma.11:1, al. ;] 
very, exceedingly: Matthieu 2:16 4:8 8:28 27:14 Marc 1:35 6:51 (Rec. λ. ἐκ περισσοῦ) Marc 9:3 16:2, Luc 23:8, 2 Timothée 4:15, II Jn 4, 3Jn.3 (cf. ὑτερλίαν).†

G3030.def:
λίβανος, -ου, ὁ
(rarely ἡ), (from the Semitic; cf. the Heb. equiv.), [in LXX for לְבוֹנָה Exode 30:34, Ésaïe 60:6; Sir.24:15, al. ;] 
__1. in cl., the frankincense-tree. 
__2. (Occas. in cl.) frankincense (so Lévitique 2:1; cf. λιβανωτός): Matthieu 2:11, Apocalypse 18:13.†

G3031.def:
λιβανωτός, -οῦ, ὁ
(λίβανος), [in LXX: 1 Chroniques 9:29, 3Ma.5:2 * ;] 
__1. in cl. (and LXX), frankincense, the gum of the libanus. 
__2. = Late Gk., λιβανωτρίς, a censer: Apocalypse 8:3, 5 (the same form appears in Inscr.; MM, xvi).†

G3032.def:
Λιβερῖτνος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. libertinus), 
a freedman: ἡ συναγωγὴ ἡ λεγομένη Λιβερτίνων Actes 6:9 (Bl. thinks the original reading was Λιβυστίνων, Phil. Gosp., 69 f.).†

G3033.def: Libya, the north part of Africa west of Egypt, (Odyssey by Homer); in later writers also for the whole Continent (ML)

G3034.def:
λιθάζω
(λίθος), [in LXX (before ἐν λίθοις): 2 Rois 16:6 16:13 (סָקַל pi.)* ;] 
__1. to throw stones (Arist., Polyb., al.). 
__2. = λιθοβολέω (LXX, NT), to pelt with stones, to stone: with accusative of person(s), Jean 8:6 10:31-31 11:8, Actes 14:10; pass., Actes 5:26, 2 Corinthiens 11:25, Hébreux 11:37 (see DB, Art., " Crimes and punish­ments," and cf. κατα-λιθάζω).†

G3035.def:
λίθινος, -η, -ον
(λίθος) [in LXX for אֶבֶן ;] 
of stone: Jean 2:6, 2 Corinthiens 3:3, Apocalypse 9:20.†

G3036.def:
λιθο-βολέω, -ῶ
(λίθος, βάλλω), [in LXX for סָקַל, רָגַם, Exode 19:13, Lévitique 20:2, al. ;] 
to pelt with stones, to kill by stoning, to stone (cf. λιθάζω): with accusative of person(s), Matthieu 21:35 23:37, Luc 13:34 Actes 7:58-59 14:5; pass., Hébreux 12:20 (LXX).†

G3037.def:
λίθος, -ου, ὁ
(and, in Att.., of precious stones, ἡ.) [in LXX for אֶבֶן, Genèse 11:3, al.; λ. τίμιος, for פָּז, Psaumes 19:10 21:3, Proverbes 8:19, al. ;] 
a stone: Matthieu 4:6, al.; pl., Matthieu 3:9, al.; at the entrance of a tomb, Matthieu 27:60, 66 28:2, Marc 15:46 16:3-4, Luc 24:2, Jean 11:38, 32 11:41 20:1; λ. μυλικός, Luc 17:2, cf. Apocalypse 18:21; of building stones, Matthieu 21:42, [44], Matthieu 24:2, Marc 12:10 13:1-2, Luc 19:44 20:17-18 21:5-6 Actes 4:11, 1 Pierre 2:7; metaphorically, of Christ, λ. ἀκρογωναῖος, ἐκλεκτός, ἔντιμος, 1 Pierre 2:6 (LXX); λ. ζῶν, 1 Pierre 2:4; προσκόμματος, 1 Pierre 2:8, Romains 9:33; of Christians, λ. ζῶντες, 1 Pierre 2:5; of precious stones, λ. τίμιος, Apocalypse 17:4 18:12, 16 21:11, 19; ἴασπις, Apocalypse 4:3; ἐνδεδυμένοι λ. καθαρόν, Apocalypse 15:6 (λίνον, Rec., R, mg., see Swete, in l); metaphorically, λ. τίμιοι, 1 Corinthiens 3:12; of the tables of the law, 2 Corinthiens 3:7; of idols, Actes 17:29

G3038.def:
λιθό-στρωτος, -ον
(στρώννυμι), [in LXX: 2 Chroniques 7:3, Esther 1:6, Cantique des cantiques 3:10 (רִצְפָּה, רָצַף)* ;] 
paved with stones, esp. of tessallated work (Ca, i.e.); as subst., τὸ λ., a tessallated pavement: Jean 19:13 (cf. Γαββαθᾶ).†

G3039.def:
λικμάω, -ῶ
(λικμός = λίκνον, a winnowing-fan), [in LXX chiefly for זָרָה ni., pi., Ruth 3:2 3Ki.14:15, Ésaïe 17:13, Jérémie 31:10, Daniel 2:44, al. ;] 
__1. in cl., to winnow (so Ru, l.with). 
__2. In LXX (ll with, exc. Ru), to scatter (as chaff or dust): Luc 20:18 (RV, scatter as dust, Deiss., BS, 225 f., quotes ex. in π. which suggests the meaning ruin, destroy; cf. Vg. comminuet, AV, grind to powder; cf. also Kennedy, Sources, 126), Matthieu 21:44 [WH], R, txt.†

G3040.def:
λιμήν, -ένος, ὁ 
[in LXX: Psaumes 107:30 (מָחוֹז), Psaumes 107:35, 1Es.5:55 Esther 5:1-2 Esther 5:1-73 4Macc 7:1-23 * ;] 
a harbour, haven: Actes 27:8, 12 (cf. Καλοὶ Λιμένες).†

G3041.def:
λίμνη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX: Psaumes 107:35 114:8 (אֲגַם), Cantique des cantiques 7:5 (בְּרֵכָה) 1Ma.11:35, 2Ma.12:16 * ;] 
a lake: of the Sea of Galilee (Mt, Mk, see: θάλασσα), Luc 5:2 8:22-23, 33; λ. Γεννησαρέτ (which see), Luc 5:1; λ. τ. πυρός, Apocalypse 19:20 20:10, 14-15; καιομένη πυρί, Apocalypse 21:8.†

G3042.def:
λιμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(so in Att..; in Dor. ἡ, and so sometimes in LXX, see Th., Gr., 146; in NT: Luc 15:14, Actes 11:28; cf. M, Pr., 60), [in LXX chiefly for רָעָב ;] 
hunger, famine: Luc 4:25 15:14, 17, Actes 7:11" (LXX) Actes 11:28, Romains 8:35, Apocalypse 6:8 18:8; λ. καὶ δίψος, 2 Corinthiens 11:27; pl., Matthieu 24:7, Marc 13:8, Luc 21:11.†

G3043.def:
λίνον
(Tr. λῖνον), -ου, τό [in LXX: Exode 9:31 (פִּשְׁתָּה), al. ;] 
__1. flax: Matthieu 12:20 (LXX). 
__2. linen: Apocalypse 15:6 (R, mg., see: λίθος).†
λίθος, -ου, ὁ
(and, in Att.., of precious stones, ἡ.) [in LXX for אֶבֶן, Genèse 11:3, al.; λ. τίμιος, for פָּז, Psaumes 19:10 21:3, Proverbes 8:19, al. ;] 
a stone: Matthieu 4:6, al.; pl., Matthieu 3:9, al.; at the entrance of a tomb, Matthieu 27:60, 66 28:2, Marc 15:46 16:3-4, Luc 24:2, Jean 11:38, 32 11:41 20:1; λ. μυλικός, Luc 17:2, cf. Apocalypse 18:21; of building stones, Matthieu 21:42, [44], Matthieu 24:2, Marc 12:10 13:1-2, Luc 19:44 20:17-18 21:5-6 Actes 4:11, 1 Pierre 2:7; metaphorically, of Christ, λ. ἀκρογωναῖος, ἐκλεκτός, ἔντιμος, 1 Pierre 2:6 (LXX); λ. ζῶν, 1 Pierre 2:4; προσκόμματος, 1 Pierre 2:8, Romains 9:33; of Christians, λ. ζῶντες, 1 Pierre 2:5; of precious stones, λ. τίμιος, Apocalypse 17:4 18:12, 16 21:11, 19; ἴασπις, Apocalypse 4:3; ἐνδεδυμένοι λ. καθαρόν, Apocalypse 15:6 (λίνον, Rec., R, mg., see Swete, in l); metaphorically, λ. τίμιοι, 1 Corinthiens 3:12; of the tables of the law, 2 Corinthiens 3:7; of idols, Actes 17:29

G3044.def:
1. Linos , a mythical minstrel, son of Apollo and Urania (Calliope), teacher of Orpheus, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus), etc. 
2. as appellative, the song or lay of Linos , sung by a boy to the cithara while the vintagers are at work, Λίνον ὑπὸ καλὸν ἄειδεν sang the lovely lay of Linos in accompaniment, (Iliad by Homer):—;compare αἴλινος which is a mournful song. (ML)

G3045.def:
λιπαρός, -ά, -όν
(λίπος, fat), [in LXX: Juges 3:29, Néhémie 9:35, Is 30:23 (שָׁמֵן)* ;] 
oily, fatty; metaphorically, of living, rich, dainty: τὰ λ. καὶ τ. λαμπρά, Apocalypse 18:14.†

G3046.def:
λίτρα, -ας, ἡ
(cf. Lat. libra), 
__1. a Sicilian coin = Rom. libra or as. 
__2. In weight, a pound: Jean 12:3 19:39.†

G3047.def:
λίψ, λιβός, ὁ
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for תֵּימָן, מַעֲרָב, etc., Genèse 13:14, Nombres 2:10, 2 Chroniques 32:30, al. ;] 
the SW. wind: βλέποντα κατὰ λ., Actes 27:12 (see Page, in l; Deiss., ES, 141).†

G3048.def:
λογία 
(prop., -εία, see BS, 142 ff.), -ας, ἡ (λογεύω, to collect, a word found in π., see Deiss., BS, l.with; LAE, 70, 103; MM, xvi), 
a collection: 1 Corinthiens 16:1-2.†

G3050.def:
λογικός, -ή, -όν
(λόγος, reason) 
reasonable, rational: λατρεία, Romains 12:1; τὸ λ. (i.e. spiritual) γάλα (see Hort, in l; MM, xvi), 1 Pierre 2:2 (in support of AV, milk of the word, see ICC, in l).†

G3051.def:
λόγιον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of λόγος, see ICC, Ro., 70), [in LXX chiefly for אִמְרָה, אֵמֶר, Psaumes 18:30 19:14, al.; also for דָּבָר, Ésaïe 28:13, al.; (cf. λογεῖον (-ιον) for חֹשֶׁן the oracular breastplate of the H.P., Exode 28:15, al.) ;] 
an oracle: Actes 7:38, Romains 3:2, Hébreux 5:12, 1 Pierre 4:11 (on the eccl., λόγια τ. Κυρίου, see Lft., Essay on Sup. Rel., 172 ff.).†

G3052.def:
λόγιος, -ον
(λόγος), 
__1. in cl., learned (Ac, l.with, R, txt.). 
__2. In late Gk., eloquent: Actes 18:24 (see Page, in l; Field, Notes, 129).†

G3053.def:
λογισμός, -οῦ, ὁ
(λογίζομαι), [in LXX: Psaumes 33:10-11, Proverbes 19:21, Ésaïe 66:18, al. (מַחֲשָׁבָה) ;] 
a reasoning, thought: Romains 2:15, 2 Corinthiens 10:5.†

G3054.def:
λογομαχέω, -ῶ
(λόγος, μάχομαι), 
to strive with words: 2 Timothée 2:14.†

G3055.def:
λογομαχία, -ας, ἡ
(λογομαχέω), 
a strife of words: pl., 1 Timothée 6:4.†

G3056.def:
λόγος, -ου, ὁ (λέγω) 
[in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר, also for מִלָּה ,אֵמֶר, etc. ;] 
__I. Of that by which the inward thought is expressed, Lat. oratio, sermo, vox, verbum. 
__1. a word, not in the grammatical sense of a mere name (ἔπος, ὄνομα, ῥῆμα), but a word as embodying a conception or idea: Matthieu 8:8, Luc 7:7, 1 Corinthiens 14:9, 19 Hébreux 12:19, al. 
__2. a saying, statement, declaration: Matthieu 19:22 (T om.), Marc 5:36 7:29, Luc 1:29, Jean 2:22 6:60, Actes 7:29, al.; with genitive attrib., Actes 13:15, Romains 9:9, Hébreux 7:28, al.; of the sayings, commands, promises, etc., of teachers, Matthieu 7:24 10:14, Marc 8:38, Luc 9:4, Jean 14:24, al.; λ. κενοί, Éphésiens 5:6; ἀληθινοί, Apocalypse 19:9; πιστοί, Apocalypse 22:6; esp. of the precepts, decrees and promises of God, ὁ λ. τ. θεοῦ, the word of God: Marc 7:13, Jean 10:35, Romains 13:9, 1 Corinthiens 14:36, Philippiens 1:14, al.; absol., ὁ λ., Matthieu 13:21, 22 Mrk.16:[20], Luc 1:2, Actes 6:4, Hébreux 4:12, al. 
__3. speech, discourse: Actes 14:12, 2 Corinthiens 10:10, Jacques 3:2; opposite to ἐπιστολή, 2 Thessaloniciens 2:15; disting, from σοφία, 1 Corinthiens 2:1; ἀναστροφή, 1 Timothée 4:12; δύναμις, 1 Corinthiens 4:19, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:5; ἔργον, Romains 15:18; οὐδενὸς λ. τίμιον (not worthy of mention), Actes 20:24; of the faculty of speech, Luc 24:19, 2 Corinthiens 11:6; of the style of speech, Matthieu 5:37, 1 Corinthiens 1:5; of instruction, Colossiens 4:3, 1 Pierre 3:1; with genitive of person(s), Jean 5:24 8:52, Actes 2:41, al.; ὁ λ. ὁ ἐμός, Jean 8:31; with genitive obj. (τ.) ἀληθείας, 2 Corinthiens 6:7, Colossiens 1:5, Jacques 1:18; τ. καταλλαγῆς, 2 Corinthiens 5:19; τ. σταυροῦ, 1 Corinthiens 1:18; of mere talk, 1 Corinthiens 4:19, 2o, Colossiens 2:23, 1 Jean 3:18; of the talk which one occasions, hence, repute: Colossiens 2:23. 
__4. subject-matter, hence, teaching, doctrine: Actes 18:15, 2 Timothée 2:17, al.; esp. of Christian doctrine: Matthieu 13:20-23, Marc 4:14-20 8:32, Luc 1:2, Actes 8:4, Galates 6:6, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:6, al.; with genitive of person(s), τ. θεοῦ, Luc 5:1, Jean 17:6, Actes 4:29, 1 Corinthiens 14:36, I Jean 1:10, Apocalypse 6:9, al.; τ. Κυρίου, Actes 8:25, 1 Thessaloniciens 1:8, al.; τ. Χριστοῦ, Colossiens 3:16, Apocalypse 3:8; with genitive appos., Actes 15:7; with genitive attrib., Hébreux 5:13. 
__5. a story, tale, narrative: Matthieu 28:15, Jean 21:23, Actes 1:1 11:22; before περί, Luc 5:15. 
__6. That which is spoken of (Plat., al.; V. Kennedy, Sources, 124), matter, affair, thing: Matthieu 21:24, Marc 1:45 11:29, Luc 20:3, Actes 8:21; of a matter in dispute, as a case or suit at law, Actes 19:38; pl. (1Ma.7:33, al.), Luc 1:4. 
__II. Of the inward thought itself, Lat. ratio. 
__1. reason, 
__(a) of the mental faculty (Hdt., Plat., al.): κατὰ λόγον, Actes 18:14; 
__(b) a reason, cause: τίνι λόγῳ, Actes 10:29; παρεκτὸς λόγου πορνείας, Matthieu 5:32 19:9, WH, mg., R, mg. 
__2. account, 
__(a) regard: Actes 20:24, Rec.; 
__(b) reckoning: Philippiens 4:15, 17; συναίρειν (which see) λ., Matthieu 18:23 25:19; in forensic sense, Romains 14:12, Hébreux 13:17, 1 Pierre 4:5; with genitive of thing(s), Luc 16:2; before περί, Matthieu 12:36, Actes 19:40, 1 Pierre 3:15. 
__3. proportion, analogy: Philippiens 2:16 (Field, Notes, 193 f.). 
__III. ὁ λ., the Divine Word or Logos: Jean 1:1, 14; τ. ζωῆς, 1 Jean 1:1; τ. θεοῦ, Apocalypse 19:13 (see Westc, Swete, CGT, in ll.; reff. in Artt., Logos, DB, DCG).

G3057.def:
λόγχη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX for רֹמַח, etc. ;] 
__1. a spear-head. 
__2. a lance, spear: Matthieu 27:49 ([WH], R, mg.), Jean 19:34.†

G3058.def:
λοιδορέω, -ῶ
(λοίδορος) [in LXX chiefly for רִיב ;] 
to abuse, revile: with accusative of person(s), Jean 9:28, Actes 23:4; pass., 1 Corinthiens 4:12, 1 Pierre 2:23 (cf. ἀντι-λοιδορέω).†

G3059.def:
λοιδορία, -ας, ἡ
(λοιδορέω), [in LXX chiefly for רִיב, מְרִיבָה ;] 
abuse, railing: 1 Timothée 5:14, 1 Pierre 3:9.†

G3060.def:
λοίδορος, -ον 
[in LXX: Proverbes 25:24 26:21 27:15 (מִדְיָן) Sir.23:8 * ;] 
railing, abusive; as subst., ὁ λ., a railer: 1 Corinthiens 5:11 6:10.†

G3061.def:
λοιμός, -οῦ, ὁ 
[in LXX for לוּץ, עָרִיץ, בְּלִיַּעַל, etc. ;] 
pestilence: pl., Luc 21:11; metaphorically (as in cl.; LXX: Psaumes 1:1, Proverbes 21:24, 1Ma.15:21, al.), of persons, a pest: Actes 24:5 (also as adj., ἄνδρες λοιμοί, 1Ma.10:61, al.).†

G3062.def:
λοιπός, -ή, -όν
(λείπω), [in LXX chiefly for יָתַר, also for שְׁאָר, etc. ;] 
the remaining, the rest, 
__1. pl., οἱ λ.: with subst., Matthieu 25:11, Actes 2:37, Romains 1:13, al.; absol., Matthieu 22:6, Marc 16:13, Luc 24:10, al.; οἱ λ. οἱ (B1., § 47, 8), Actes 28:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:13, Apocalypse 2:24; οἱ λ. τ. ἀνθρώπων (LS, see word, ad. init.), Apocalypse 9:20; τὰ λ., Marc 4:19, Apocalypse 3:2, al. 
__2. Neut. sing. (accusative ref.), adverbially, τὸ λ.; 
__(a) for the future, henceforth: Marc 14:41, 1 Corinthiens 7:29 (Lft., Notes, 232 f.), Hébreux 10:13; anarth. (Deiss., LAE, 17616, 1885, 20), Actes 27:20, 2 Timothée 4:8; τοῦ λ. (sc. χρόνου; LS, see word; M, Pr., 73; Bl., § 36, 13), Galates 6:17, Éphésiens 6:10; 
__(b) besides, moreover, for the rest: Philippiens 3:1 4:8; anarth., 1 Corinthiens 1:16 4:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:1 (M, Th., in l; Lft., Notes, 51)

G3063.def:
λοιπός, -ή, -όν
(λείπω), [in LXX chiefly for יָתַר, also for שְׁאָר, etc. ;] 
the remaining, the rest, 
__1. pl., οἱ λ.: with subst., Matthieu 25:11, Actes 2:37, Romains 1:13, al.; absol., Matthieu 22:6, Marc 16:13, Luc 24:10, al.; οἱ λ. οἱ (B1., § 47, 8), Actes 28:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:13, Apocalypse 2:24; οἱ λ. τ. ἀνθρώπων (LS, see word, ad. init.), Apocalypse 9:20; τὰ λ., Marc 4:19, Apocalypse 3:2, al. 
__2. Neut. sing. (accusative ref.), adverbially, τὸ λ.; 
__(a) for the future, henceforth: Marc 14:41, 1 Corinthiens 7:29 (Lft., Notes, 232 f.), Hébreux 10:13; anarth. (Deiss., LAE, 17616, 1885, 20), Actes 27:20, 2 Timothée 4:8; τοῦ λ. (sc. χρόνου; LS, see word; M, Pr., 73; Bl., § 36, 13), Galates 6:17, Éphésiens 6:10; 
__(b) besides, moreover, for the rest: Philippiens 3:1 4:8; anarth., 1 Corinthiens 1:16 4:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:1 (M, Th., in l; Lft., Notes, 51)

G3064.def:
λοιπός, -ή, -όν
(λείπω), [in LXX chiefly for יָתַר, also for שְׁאָר, etc. ;] 
the remaining, the rest, 
__1. pl., οἱ λ.: with subst., Matthieu 25:11, Actes 2:37, Romains 1:13, al.; absol., Matthieu 22:6, Marc 16:13, Luc 24:10, al.; οἱ λ. οἱ (B1., § 47, 8), Actes 28:9, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:13, Apocalypse 2:24; οἱ λ. τ. ἀνθρώπων (LS, see word, ad. init.), Apocalypse 9:20; τὰ λ., Marc 4:19, Apocalypse 3:2, al. 
__2. Neut. sing. (accusative ref.), adverbially, τὸ λ.; 
__(a) for the future, henceforth: Marc 14:41, 1 Corinthiens 7:29 (Lft., Notes, 232 f.), Hébreux 10:13; anarth. (Deiss., LAE, 17616, 1885, 20), Actes 27:20, 2 Timothée 4:8; τοῦ λ. (sc. χρόνου; LS, see word; M, Pr., 73; Bl., § 36, 13), Galates 6:17, Éphésiens 6:10; 
__(b) besides, moreover, for the rest: Philippiens 3:1 4:8; anarth., 1 Corinthiens 1:16 4:2, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:1 (M, Th., in l; Lft., Notes, 51)

G3065.def:
Λουκᾶς, -ᾶ, ὁ
(prob. an abbreviation of Λουκανός; see Lft., Col., 240; ICC, Lk., xviii; Bl., § 29; accusative to Ramsay, Exp., Dec., 1912, pp. 502 ff., a by-form of Λούκιος, from Lat. Lucius), 
Luke: Lk, tit., Colossiens 4:14, 2 Timothée 4:11, Phm 24.†

G3066.def:
λούκιος, -ου, ὁ (Lat. Lucius), 
Lucius: Actes 13:1, Romains 16:21.†

G3067.def:
λουτρόν, -οῦ, τό
(λούω), [in LXX: Cantique des cantiques 4:2 6:5, (6) (רַחְצָה), Sir.34:25 * ;] 
a washing, bath: τ. ὕδατος, Éphésiens 5:26; τ. παλιγγενεσίας, Tite 3:5 (see AR, Eph., l.with).†

G3068.def:
λούω 
[in LXX chiefly for רָחַץ (frequently of ceremonial washing; cf. Deiss., BS, 226 f.) ;] 
to bathe, wash the body: with accusative of person(s), Actes 9:37 (of a dead body); id. before ἀπό (Deiss., BS, l.with), Actes 16:33; pass. ptcp. pf., Jean 13:10, Hébreux 10:22; mid., to wash oneself (Mayor, in l; M. Pr., 155 f., 238 f.), 2 Pierre 2:22; metaphorically, Apocalypse 1:5, Rec., R, mg. (cf. ἀπο-λούω).†
SYN.: νίπτω, used of parts of the body-hands, feet, face; πλύνω, of things, as garments, etc. (see Lévitique 15:11; cf. Tr., Syn., § xlv)

G3069.def:
λύδδα, -ας (Actes 9:38, -ης Rec.), ἡ and λύδδα, -ων, τά (Actes 9:32, 35; -αν, Rec.), (Heb. לֹד), 
Lydda (modern Ludd): Ac, ll. with†

G3070.def:
Λυδία, -ας, ἡ 
Lydia, a woman of Thyatira: Actes 16:14, 40.†

G3071.def:
Λυκαονία, -ας, ἡ 
Lycaonia, a region in Asia Minor: Actes 14:6.†

G3073.def:
Λυκία, -ας, ἡ 
Lydia, a region of Asia Minor; Actes 27:5.†

G3074.def:
λύκος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for זְאֵב ;] 
a wolf: Matthieu 10:16, Luc 10:3, Jean 10:12; figuratively (as Eze.22:27, Sophonie 3:3, Jérémie 5:6, al.), Matthieu 7:1, Actes 20:29.†

G3075.def:
λυμαίνομαι
(λύμη, outrage), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁחַת pi., hi., also for כִּרְסֵם, etc. ;] 
__1. to outrage, maltreat: with accusative, Actes 8:3. 
__2. to corrupt, defile (Eze.16:25, Proverbes 23:8, 4Ma.18:8, al.).†

G3076.def:
λυπέω, -ῶ
(λύπη), [in LXX for חָרָה, etc. ;] 
to distress, grieve, cause pain or grief: with accusative of person(s), 2 Corinthiens 2:2 2:5 7:8; pass., Matthieu 14:9 17:23 18:31 19:22 26:22, Marc 10:22 14:19, Jean 16:20 21:17, Romains 14:15, 2 Corinthiens 2:4, 1 Thessaloniciens 4:13, 1 Pierre 1:6; λ. καὶ ἀδημονεῖν, Matthieu 26:37; opposite to χαίρειν, 2 Corinthiens 6:10; κατὰ θεόν, 2 Corinthiens 7:9 7:11; τ. πνεῦμα τ. ἅγιον, Éphésiens 4:30 (cf. συν-λνπέω),†
SYN.: see: θρηνέω

G3077.def:
λύπη, -ης, ἡ 
[in LXX for עֶצֶב and cogn. forms, etc. ;] 
pain of body or mind, grief, sorrow: Jean 16:6, 2 Corinthiens 2:7; opposite to χαρά, Jean 16:20, Hébreux 12:11; ἀπὸ τῆς λ., Luc 22:45; ἐκ λ., 2 Corinthiens 9:7; ἡ κατὰ θεὸν λ., opposite to ἡ τ. κόσ-μου λ., 2 Corinthiens 7:10; λ. μοι ἐστιν, Romains 9:2; λ. ἔχω, Jean 16:21-22; id. before ἀπό, 2 Corinthiens 2:3; λ. ἐπὶ λ. ἔχω, Philippiens 2:27; ἐν λ. ἐλθεῖν, 2 Corinthiens 2:1 (to come sad and cause sadness); pl. (cf. Genèse 3:16, Proverbes 15:13, al.), 1 Pierre 2:19.†

G3079.def:
Λυσίας, -ου, ὁ
Lysias (Claudius L., Actes 23:26), Actes 24:7, 22.†

G3080.def:
λύσις, -εως, ἡ
(λύω), [in LXX: Ecclésiaste 8:1 (Ecclésiaste 8:1) (פֵּשֶׁר), Dan LXX 12:8, Wis.8:8 * ;] 
a loosing: of divorce, 1 Corinthiens 7:27.†

G3081.def:
λυσιτελέω, -ῶ
(λυσιτελής, useful, prop., τὰ τέλη λύων), [in LXX: Tob.3:6, Sir.20:10, 14 29:11 * ;] 
__1. prop., to indemnify, pay expenses. 
__2. to be useful, to profit; usually impers., λυσιτελεῖ, it profits: with, dative of person(s), before εἰ . . . ἤ, Luc 17:2.†

G3082.def:
λύστρα, -ας, ἡ 
and (in Actes 14:8 16:2, 2Ti, l.with) -ων, τά (cf. Λύδδα), 
Lystra, a city of Lycaonia: Actes 14:6, 8 14:21 16:1-2, 2 Timothée 3:11.†

G3083.def:
λύτρον, -ον, τό
(λύω), [in LXX (Pent. .15 Pr .2, Isa .1) for פִּדְיוֹם and cogn. forms, גְּאֻלָּה, כֹּפֶר, מְחִיר ;] 
a ransom (as for a life, Exode 21:30; for slaves, Lévitique 19:20; for captives, Ésaïe 45:13): ἀντὶ πολλῶν, Matthieu 20:28, Marc 10:45 (see Swete, in l, and for discussion of λ. and its cognates, Westc., He., 295 f.; Deiss., LAE, 331 f.; cf. also ἀντί-λύτρον).†

G3084.def:
λυτρόω, -ῶ
(λύτρον, which see), [in LXX chiefly for פָּדָה, גָּאַל ;] 
to release on receipt of ransom; mid., to release by paying ransom, to redeem: in spiritual sense, Tite 2:14; pass, 1 Pierre 1:18; in general sense, to deliver (cf. Exode 6:6, Psaumes 69:18, al.): Luc 24:21.†

G3085.def:
λύτρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(λυτρόω), [in LXX: Lévitique 25:29, 48, Ésaïe 63:4 גְּאֻלָּה), Nombres 18:16, Psaumes 49:8 111:9 130:7 (פָּדָה, פִּדְיוֹם, פְּדוּת), Juges 1:15 * ;] 
a ransoming, redemption (αἰχμαλώτων, Plut., Arat., 11): of the mediatorial work of Christ, Hébreux 9:12; in general sense, deliverance(cf. Psaumes 4:8, l.with): Luc 1:68 2:38.†

G3086.def:
λυτρωτής, -οῦ, ὁ
(λυτρόω), [in LXX: of God, Psaumes 19:14 78:35 (גָּאַל)* ;] 
a redeemer, deliverer: Actes 7:35 (not found elsewhere).†

G3087.def:
λυχνία, -ας, ἡ
(vulgar form of λυχνίον = λυχνοῦχος; see Kennedy, Sources, 40), [in LXX for מְנוֹרָה (Exode 25:31 40:4, al.) ;] 
a lampstand: Matthieu 5:15, Marc 4:21, Luc 8:16 11:33; of that in the Tabernacle, Hébreux 9:2; metaphorically, of the two witnesses, Apocalypse 11:4; of the seven churches of Asia, Apocalypse 1:12-13, 20 2:1; of the removal of a church from its position, κινεῖν τ. λυχνίαν κ.τ.λ., Apocalypse 2:5.†

G3088.def:
λύχνος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for נִיר (Exode 25:37), al.) ;] 
a lamp (portable, and usually set on a stand, λυχνία): Matthieu 5:15, Luc 11:36; ἔρχεται ὁ λ., Marc 4:21; λ. ἅπτειν Luc 8:16 11:33 15:8; φῶς λύχνου, Apocalypse 18:23; id. opposite to φ.ἡλίου, Apocalypse 22:5; metaphorically, of the eye, Matthieu 6:22 Luc 11:34; of John the Baptist, Jean 5:35; of the Lamb, Apocalypse 21:23; of prophecy, 2 Pierre 1:19; of spiritual readiness, pl., λύχνοι (as always in LXX; frequently in Att.. λύχνα), Luc 12:35.†
SYN.: λαμπάς, q.v

G3089.def:
λύω 
[in LXX for פָּתַח, נָתַר hi., etc. ;] 
__1. to loose, unbind, release: of things, Marc 1:7, Luc 3:16, al.; of beasts, Matthieu 21:2, Luc 13:15, al.; of persons, Jean 11:44, Actes 22:30; of Satan, Apocalypse 20:3, 7; metaphorically, of the marriage tie, 1 Corinthiens 7:27; of one diseased, Luc 13:16; of release from sin, Apocalypse 1:5, WH, R, txt. (see: λούω). 
__2. To resolve a whole into its parts, loosen, dissolve, break up, destroy: Jean 2:19, Actes 27:41, Apocalypse 5:2; metaphorically, 2 Pierre 3:11; of an assembly, to dismiss: Actes 13:43; τ. μεσότοιχον τ. φραγμοῦ, Éphésiens 2:14; τ. στοιχεῖα, 2 Pierre 3:10; οὐρανοί, 2 Pierre 3:12; τ. ἔργα τ. διαβόλου, 1 Jean 3:8; τ. ὠδῖνας τ. θανάτου, Actes 2:24; of laws, etc., to break, annul, cancel (MM, xvi): ἐντολήν, Matthieu 5:19; τ. νόμον, Jean 7:23; τ. σάββατον, Jean 5:18; τ. γραφήν, Jean 10:35. 
(cf. ἀνα-, ἀπο-, δια-, ἐκ-, ἐπι-, κατα-, παρα-λύω.)

G3091.def:
Λώτ, ὁ (Heb. לוֹט), indecl., 
Lot (Genèse 11:27, al.): Luc 17:28-29, 32, 2 Pierre 2:7.†

G3093.def:
Μαγαδάν
Magadan, an unidentified place on the coast of the Sea of Galilee: Matthieu 15:39 (Rec. Μαγδαλά; cf. Marc 8:10, where for Δαλμανουθά, D* has Μελεγαδά, D1 Μαγαιδά, some cursives Μαγαδά, and Euseb. Onomast. Μεγαιδάν; cf. DB, iii, see word).†
Μαγδαλά (Aram. מַגְדְֺּלָא = Heb. H4026, which in Josué 15:37 B is rendered Μαγαδά), 
Magdala: Matthieu 15:39 (Rec. for Μαγαδάν, which see).†

G3094.def:
Μαγδαληνός, -ά, όν 
Magdalene, of Magdala: Μαρία (which see) ἡ MM., Matthieu 27:56, 61 28:1, Marc 15:40, 47 16:1, 9, Luc 8:2 24:10, Jean 19:25 20:1, 18†

G3095.def:
μαγία (Rec. -εία), -ας, ἡ 
(μάγος), 
__1. the lore of the Magians (Plat.). 
__2. magic: pl., magic arts, sorceries: Actes 8:11.†

G3096.def:
μαγεύω (Eur., Plut., al.), 
__1. to be a Magus, or skilled in Magian lore. 
__2. to practise magic: Actes 8:9.†

G3097.def:
μάγος, -ου, ὁ 
[in LXX for אַשָּׁף, Dan LXX TH Daniel 2:2, 10, al. (cf. chief magian, Jérémie 39:3, 13) ;] 
__1. one of the Μάγοι, a Median tribe (Hat). 
__2. a Magian, one of a sacred caste, originally Median, who seem to have conformed to the Persian religion, while retaining some of their old beliefs (see DB, I vol., 565 f.; DB, iii, 203 ff.): Matthieu 2:1, 7 2:16 
__3. a wizard, sorcerer: Actes 13:6, 8 (cf. Wis.17:7, Actes 8:9; ?Actes 8:1).†

G3098.def:
Μαγώγ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. מָגוֹג, Genèse 10:2, Exode 38:2, al.), 
Magog, associated with Gog: Apocalypse 20:8 (see Swete, in l).†

G3099.def:
Μαδιάμ, ὁ indecl. (Heb. מִדְיָן), 
Midian; 
__1. son of Abraham (Genèse 25:2). 
__2. An Arabian tribe (Genèse 36:35, Psaumes 83:9, al). 
__3. γῆ Μ. (Heb. מִדְיָן אֶרֶץ), the land of Midian (Exode 2:15, al.): Actes 7:29.†
